beats.text: The pyramid builders were not slaves.
beats.note: Harvard Magazine reported Mark Lehner's discovery of the city of the pyramid builders, and put it plainly.

beats.text: Herodotus gets the credit for the slave story.
beats.note: AP says he described the builders as slaves. A translation quoted by Ancient Origins says that passage uses no word for slaves.

beats.name: The workers' graves
beats.role: First found in the backyard of the Giza pyramids, according to AP. Hawass said the dead were buried near their pharaohs' pyramids.

beats.note: Harvard says early graffiti named gangs such as Friends of Khufu and Drunkards of Menkaure.

beats.context: Plus 23 sheep, sent in every day for about 10,000 labourers, according to AP in 2010. The team also found the oldest bakery ever found in Egypt.

beats.note: AP reports skeletons with arthritis and strained lower backs. Hawass said most fractures had healed well, indicating splints.

beats.text: Fed, housed and buried beside the king's pyramid.
